title: DEFA: Efficient Deformable Attention Acceleration via Pruning-Assisted Grid-Sampling and Multi-Scale Parallel Processing
problem: Multi-scale deformable attention (MSDeformAttn) suffers from irregular data access patterns and enormous memory requirements, causing severe processing element under-utilization. Existing attention acceleration approaches cannot be directly applied to MSDeformAttn due to its distinct procedural characteristics.
motivation: MSDeformAttn has demonstrated explicit superiority in various vision tasks through multi-scale grid-sampling, making efficient hardware acceleration critical for practical deployment.
method: DEFA tackles multi-scale deformable attention (a neural network mechanism focusing on different spatial regions at multiple scales) which normally wastes memory and creates irregular data access. First, it prunes feature maps (intermediate data) based on frequency and sampling points based on probability, cutting memory by over 80%. Second, it processes multiple scales in parallel, combines fine-grained operations to reduce memory transfers, and reuses data—together keeping processors busy and reducing irregular memory access.
key_novelty: DEFA combines algorithm optimizations (pruning to reduce spatial sampling) with custom hardware design (parallel multi-scale processing) specifically for multi-scale deformable attention.
contributions: Frequency-weighted and probability-aware pruning techniques reducing memory footprint by over 80%
Multi-scale parallel architecture design for improved throughput
Fine-grained layer fusion and feature map reusing strategies
Achieves 10.1-31.9X speedup and 20.3-37.7X energy efficiency improvement over GPU platforms
limitations: Design trade-offs and scalability beyond tested benchmarks not discussed
